messages:
Alex: Hey team — I'm stuck in the airport TSA line, flight delayed. I was scheduled primary for the 00:00-04:00 UTC window. There's an active pager right now for model-serving. I can't reliably take the bridge. Can someone take primary immediately and I'll hand off context?
incident-bot: PAGER triggered: model-serving-prod HIGH_ERROR_RATE (500s) — affected routes: /generate, /chat. Priority: P1. Pager link: https://pager.redwood.example/p/12345 (automated)
Meera: I can take primary for the next 4h. On-call handover: I'll open the bridge and run the quick mitigation steps. @Alex update the rotation in the calendar please. :raised_hands:
Dan: I can be secondary/backup shadow for the window. If Meera needs help with scale adjustments or to bounce a worker I can join.
Alex: thank you both. Quick context: users see 500s after ~200ms of CPU stall on model workers, likely KV cache thrash after a rollout. Recent canary deployed 3 hours ago (model v2.3.1-quant).
Meera: copying runbook snippets. Steps I'm going to try first: 1) roll back canary to v2.3.0 on the canary pool 2) increase model-worker replicas temporarily 3) enable prefix-KV cache fallback. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.example/runbooks/model-serving-p1
Meera: Running rollback now. Command:```bash
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/model-worker model-worker=redwood/model:v2.3.0-canary-safe
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/model-worker
```
incident-bot: Bridge opened: https://meet.redwood.example/bridge/abc123 (created by Meera)
Jess: Heads up — I just checked tracing. Lots of requests spiking on worker-7 with repeated KV cache misses. We should avoid a full restart if possible, cause cold-start token cost.
Meera: Rollback in progress — kubectl shows rollout progressing. If rollback doesn't reduce 500s in 5 mins, I'll scale worker pool and redirect a fraction of traffic to Dedicated pool.
Dan: If you scale, use the autoscale override script I left in ops-scripts:```bash
./scale-model-pool --pool canary --replicas 10 --reason "emergency-overnight"
```
Meera: Doing scale override now. Also enabling degraded-mode routing to send 15% traffic to smaller, older variant (v2.2.x). Config update:```json
{"routing_policy":"degraded","percentage":15,"target_model":"v2.2.9"}
```
Harry: FYI I'm watching customer-impact slack and added a short status blurb to the CS triage so they can notify impacted customers. Link: https://cs.redwood.example/ticket/7890
Meera: Rollback finished, rollout status: SUCCESS. Preliminary metrics show 500s dropped from 18% -> 2% on canary pool. Still keeping scaled replicas for 10m to observe.
Dan: Nice. Can we run a quick smoke on /chat with 50 concurrent short requests to confirm latency? I can run from my laptop:```bash
wrk -t2 -c50 -d15s http://canary-inference.local/chat -s smoke.lua
```
Meera: Smoke shows p95 under 420ms, errors <1%. I'm going to notify incident-bot to update pager status to investigating->mitigated and then handover to Alex for remaining window if needed.
incident-bot: Pager update: status changed to MITIGATED by Meera. Metrics link: https://metrics.redwood.example/d/abc/model-serving
Alex: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick cover and clear notes. Meera, please keep being primary until 02:00 UTC, then I'll take back if everything stays green. Dan/Jess, please stay on call for 30m for post-mortem artefacts.
Meera: Will do. Quick post-incident todos: 1) run KV cache analysis 2) add a canary rollback automation to reduce manual steps 3) update runbook snippet with the scale override command. I'll open follow-up issues.
Jess: I'll capture traces and add them to the incident thread. Also adding a short blameless note about deployment timing and canary config.
Dan: If anyone needs me I'm on pager and reachable via DM.
Alex: Updated calendar and rotation. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
